Take a history. Examine. Reason it through. Miss nothing.

HistoryOsis is a structured clinical intake app. Tap through the questions a good history needs, log examination signs as chips across 23 body systems, and see a ranked differential that always keeps the dangerous causes in view. It runs in your browser, works offline after the first load, and keeps records on your own device.

No account. No internet needed after the first load. Records stay on the device they were typed on. Open beta, in active testing. Advisory tool: clinical judgement and local protocols always apply.

One app for the ward round and the clinic with no internet

The same structured intake serves two very different needs. Choose the one that sounds like you.

Students and trainees

An active-recall companion for wards and OSCEs

Instead of rereading a checklist, you recall and record. The app lays out every question and examination step in the order a clinician thinks, so a thorough history becomes a habit and nothing gets missed.

  • Tap structured finding chips to log signs in real time as you examine.
  • Student mode adds teaching hints and a "Before you finish" checklist.
  • Red-flag lists and Must-not-miss causes train you to ask the question that matters.
  • Supervisors can comment on any section, then approve and lock the record.
Launch Live App — No Sign-up Required
Low-resource clinics and hospitals

Offline-ready clinical records on the devices you already have

There is no server to set up, no licence to buy to try it, and no connection to lose. It runs on phones, tablets and budget PCs, and saves records in the browser's local storage on that device.

  • Works after the first load with no internet, including all medical content.
  • Records stay on the device. Nothing is sent to us, and there are no accounts.
  • Clinician mode is lean: fewer prompts, with safety alerts always shown.
  • Print a black-and-white A4 record, a discharge summary, or copy as text.

Be aware: records live on one device and are not encrypted by the app. Use device encryption and a screen lock. Sharing between devices is not built yet.

What's new

Thirty-seven updates so far, grouped into the four things you will notice. The latest is v3.37.1. All screens and examples use fictional patients.

Examination

Enhanced physical exam coverage

  • 23 examination systems as grouped tap chips: cardiovascular, respiratory, abdomen, neurological, psychiatric, eye, ENT, thyroid, breast, skin, groin, obstetric, paediatric and more.
  • Musculoskeletal screens for GALS, hip, knee, ankle and foot, shoulder, hand and wrist, and cervical and lumbar spine.
  • Red-flag signs raise an alert, and "Mark all normal" never touches sensitive or special tests.
  • One-tap "Suggested for your complaint" exam buttons.
  • Numeric lab values with units and Normal, High, Low and Critical flags.
Reasoning

Dynamic DDx logic

  • A rule-based differential for all 76 complaints, from chest pain to fever in a child.
  • Must-not-miss causes kept visible in Student and Clinician mode.
  • Live updates as you tap, in under 15 ms on average for several complaints at once.
  • Student mode shows the reasoning. Clinician mode shows a compact list.
Documentation

Streamlined export and discharge

  • A discharge summary pre-filled from the record, with medications marked New, Changed, Continued or Stopped.
  • Allergy warnings on discharge medicines, and explicit "None recorded" where a field is empty.
  • Redesigned black-and-white A4 print that photocopies cleanly.
  • Print or save as PDF, copy text, or download a .txt file.
Experience

Performance and accessibility

  • A new home screen with Resume draft and recent records, plus bottom navigation.
  • Student and Clinician modes, eight colour presets, a custom colour, dark mode and High contrast.
  • Forced-colours support, 400% zoom without sideways scrolling, 44 px touch targets, labelled regions for screen readers.
  • One-tap Undo after removals, and an install prompt for offline use.
See every release

Open beta: help us make it safer and sharper

HistoryOsis is in open beta and gets better with every real-world edge case. We are inviting three groups to work with us.

  • Clinicians to test examination and differential content against real practice, and tell us what is wrong or missing.
  • Medical students to use it on wards and in OSCE practice, and tell us where it slows you down.
  • Front-end developers to report bugs, review accessibility and collaborate on upcoming clinical workflows.

Use fictional patients while testing. Clinical content is draft until reviewed.

Home/App tour

A tour of the app, one screen at a time

These are real screens from v3.37.1, captured with a fictional patient. The order follows a clinical encounter: start, take the history, examine, reason, check, sign off and discharge.

Light or dark? The screens follow this site's theme. Use the Theme button at the top of any page to switch.

Start

Open the app on a phone and you land on Home. Bottom navigation takes you between Home, the Intake form and your saved Records.

Take the history

Each presenting complaint opens its own questions as taps. For symptoms, one tap is present and two is absent.

Examine

Vital signs get plain-word tags as you type them. Examination systems are grouped chips, with red-flag alerts.

Reason it through

The differential panel reads what you have entered and keeps the dangerous causes in view. You choose what to add.

Check before you prescribe

Warnings are advisory. They ask you to confirm that you checked, and they never stop a record from saving.

Review and sign off

A supervisor or consultant can comment, approve and lock a record. Every step is logged.

Discharge

A discharge summary is filled in from the record. You edit it, then print, save as PDF, copy the text or download a .txt file.

Make it yours

Choose a colour preset or your own colour, switch to dark, raise contrast or text size. Printing always uses a plain light page.

Try it on your own phone

There is no account and nothing to install. Open the app, start a patient, and add it to your home screen if you want it offline.

Home/Features

Everything the app does, in the order a clinician works

From the first question to the discharge summary. Every feature on this page is in the app today.

Light or dark? The screens follow this site's theme. Use the Theme button at the top of any page to switch.

One record, seven sections, A to G

The form follows the order a clinician thinks in. Each section opens and closes, and the app shows how complete the record is as you go.

  1. A

    Demographics

    Patient ID and admission details.

  2. B

    Structured history

    Presenting complaints with tap-to-answer HOPI, review of systems, comorbidities, past medical and surgical history, family and social history. Child and pregnancy sections appear only when they apply.

  3. C

    Examination

    Vital signs with BMI, Shock Index and NEWS2, general findings, and 23 body systems of tap chips.

  4. D

    Investigations

    Bedside tests, laboratory, imaging, endoscopy and biopsy, with results.

  5. E

    Treatment plan

    Diagnosis, medical, surgical and conservative items, monitoring, discharge criteria and counselling points.

  6. F

    Signing credentials

    Who took the history: role, name, roll number, year, ward and supervisor.

  7. G

    Review and save

    The written summary, print and copy options, reviewer comments and sign-off.

What the app does at the bedside

Every feature here is in the app today. All screens show fictional patients and follow this site's theme.

Every question on the screen

Each of the 76 presenting complaints opens a set of questions as taps: onset, character, radiation, severity, duration, triggers, and what is present or absent. Nothing to remember and nothing skipped, and the record reads as if a clinician wrote it.

  • Five answer types: pick one, pick several, a 0 to 10 scale, a duration, and present or absent.
  • Red-flag lists for 15 complaints, folded away until you need them.
  • Search for a complaint, pin favourites and reuse recent ones.
  • Eight templates, such as a chest pain work-up or a sepsis screen, add the usual complaints, examination, tests and plan in one tap. Save your own.
  • Returning patient: carry stable history forward from an earlier record.

Examine with taps, and see red flags as you go

Examination is grouped chips across 23 body systems. Tap the signs you find, or mark a system normal in one tap. Red-flag signs raise an alert.

  • Cardiovascular, respiratory, abdomen, neurological, psychiatric, eye, ENT, thyroid, breast, skin, groin, obstetric, paediatric and more.
  • Musculoskeletal screens for GALS, hip, knee, ankle and foot, shoulder, hand and wrist, and cervical and lumbar spine.
  • "Mark all normal" never touches sensitive or special tests.
  • Numeric lab values with units and Normal, High, Low and Critical flags.

Draft content. Examination content is labelled Draft until a named clinician has reviewed each system.

See the sick patient sooner

As vitals are typed, each gets a plain-word tag: normal, abnormal or critical. NEWS2 adds up the score on the Royal College of Physicians chart, shows the risk band and the suggested response, and saves it with the record.

  • Reads vitals the way people type them: 96 bpm, 97%, 5'10", 150 lbs.
  • Respiratory rate, SpO₂ (including Scale 2), blood pressure, pulse, temperature and GCS.
  • Shock Index and BMI worked out for you.
  • Tags use words as well as colour, so they work for everyone.

Decision support only. Every check is advisory and never blocks saving. Clinical judgement and local protocols apply.

A differential that keeps the dangerous causes in view

The panel reads the history, signs, vitals and flagged results you have entered and lists possibilities to consider. Must-not-miss causes come first and stay visible.

  • A rule-based list for all 76 presenting complaints. It is not AI.
  • Each candidate shows what supports it, what argues against it and what is not yet known.
  • One tap adds a candidate to your differentials, with Undo. Nothing is added on its own.

How the differential works

Catch the allergy before the prescription

If allergies have not been recorded, a banner says so. If a chosen medicine clashes with a recorded allergy, the warning appears on that medicine and asks you to confirm that you checked.

  • 33 medicines mapped to drug groups, including related groups.
  • 16 condition cautions, such as an anti-inflammatory in kidney disease or alongside an anticoagulant.
  • A "Before you finish" checklist: allergies, diagnosis, vitals, and confirmation of carried-forward allergies and medicines.
  • The clinician stays in charge. Warnings never stop a record from being saved.

From bedside to record in one tap

The form turns into a written summary, an A4 printout or plain text for another system. Records stay easy to find and hard to lose.

  • Summary view, with print or PDF in full and compact layouts.
  • A discharge summary pre-filled from the record, with print, PDF, copy-text and .txt export.
  • Share a text summary, or copy the record as EMR text.
  • Search, filter and tag. Status: Draft, Complete or Discharged.
  • The last 10 versions of each record are kept. Deleted records wait in a trash until you restore them.
  • Download a backup file, and upload one with a preview before anything is merged.

Review and sign-off built in

Supervisors and consultants comment on any section of the record. When the author marks it ready, the reviewer approves it and the record becomes read-only until someone reopens it. Every step is logged with name, role and time.

  • Comments live inside the record, under the section they are about.
  • Open comments show on the records list, so nothing is missed.
  • Approval warns if comments are still open.
  • Works for teaching rounds and for ward sign-off.

Comfortable on every shift

Light, dark or automatic theme for night shifts, three text sizes, and labels for screen readers and keyboards. It runs on phones, tablets and computers, and installs to the home screen.

  • Works offline after the first load.
  • PIN lock and privacy screen for a device left on a ward desk.
  • Eight colour presets, a custom colour and High contrast. Student and Clinician modes.
  • Content and calculations checked by automated tests that run in any browser.

Home/Differentials

How the differential diagnosis works

Form hypotheses, then look for what supports or excludes them. The panel does this at the bedside for all 76 presenting complaints.

Light or dark? The screens follow this site's theme. Use the Theme button at the top of any page to switch.

A differential that reasons the way you do

The differential diagnosis engine reads the history you tapped, the signs you found, the vitals and the lab and imaging results, and turns them into a prioritised list at the bedside. It follows hypothetico-deductive reasoning: form hypotheses, then look for what supports or excludes each one.

  1. It listens to everything you enterHistory chips, red flags, examination findings, vitals, flagged lab values, risk factors, age and sex.
  2. It never hides the dangerous causes"Must not miss" always comes first and stays visible, even when other findings point away from it.
  3. It tells you what to ask or check next"To tell these apart" suggests the discriminating question, and "Tests that may help" adds a test in one tap.
  4. You stay in chargeOne tap adds a candidate to your differentials, with Undo. Nothing is added or overwritten on its own.

Decision support, not a diagnosis. The engine is rule-based, not AI. It covers all 76 presenting complaints with more than 165 test vignettes. The content is draft and awaiting review by named clinicians. Always apply clinical judgement and local protocols.

Chest pain

Draft

Possibilities to consider, not a diagnosis. Fictional example.

⚠ Must not miss

  • Acute coronary syndrome (supported)
  • Pulmonary embolism
  • Aortic dissection

Fits the findings so far

  • Acute coronary syndrome
  • Stable angina

To tell these apart

  • Pain pleuritic or positional?
  • Blood pressure difference between arms?

Tests that may help

  • ECG, troponin, D-dimer

How to read the panel

The panel sits in Section E of the record. Each candidate opens to show its reasoning.

Must not miss
Dangerous causes, listed first and always visible in Student and Clinician mode.
Supported by
Only the findings this patient actually has, such as "radiation to the arm or jaw".
Argues against (does not exclude)
Findings that point away. They never remove a candidate.
Not yet known
What you have not asked or examined yet, so you know what is missing.
To tell these apart
The question or examination that best separates the candidates.
Tests that may help
Add a test to the investigations list in one tap.
Student and Clinician mode
Student mode shows the reasoning. Clinician mode shows a compact list.

What it is, and what it is not

Rule-based, not AI

Every rule is written down, cited from standard teaching and tested against vignettes. The same entries always give the same list.

Possibilities, not a diagnosis

Decision support only. It never decides, never blocks saving, and never overwrites what you wrote.

Draft until a clinician signs it off

The content is labelled Draft and awaits review by named clinicians. Use clinical judgement and local protocols.

Try the chest pain case

Open the app, add Chest Pain and tap through the questions. The panel updates as you go.

Three settings, one app

Medical schools use it to teach. Small clinics use it as their patient record. Hospital wards use it on rounds. Pick the one that sounds like you.

Put the same checklist in every student's pocket.

Students practise on their own phones, offline, with the questions a good history needs already laid out. Supervisors see what is missing and comment on the record itself.

  • 76 presenting complaints with tap-to-answer questions, and red-flag lists for the dangerous ones, so no question is forgotten.
  • A completeness checklist for every section shows what the student has not covered yet.
  • Reviewer mode: comment on any section, mark a record ready, then approve and lock it.
  • A sign-off block records student name, roll number, year, ward and supervisor.
  • A case log you can download as a spreadsheet (CSV) to show the cases a student has seen.
  • Your faculty's own complaints, questions and templates go into one content file.

Next for teaching: a history coverage score, practice cases with an OSCE timer, and a student logbook. Examination and differential content is labelled Draft until a named clinician has reviewed each system.

A proper patient record on the phone or computer you already have.

There is no server to set up and no monthly login. Open the app, take the history, save the record, then print it or copy it into another system.

  • A structured record from demographics to treatment plan, saved on the device and available offline.
  • Returning patient? Load the stable history from the earlier record with the same MR number, then reconfirm allergies and medicines.
  • Search by name, MR number, bed, diagnosis or tag. Mark records Draft, Complete or Discharged.
  • Print a full or compact A4 record, share a text summary, or copy it as EMR text.
  • Version history, a recently deleted view with restore, and backup reminders with a one-tap backup file.
  • Installs on the home screen like any other app.

Today: records live on one device. Sharing records between devices and staff is on the roadmap. Use device encryption and a screen lock on any phone that holds real patient records.

Faster, safer ward rounds, one bed at a time.

Round view and early-warning scores for the ward, and sign-off for the record. Hospital-wide deployment is what we are building with pilot partners.

  • Round view with progress notes (SOAP) that show yesterday's vitals, examination and plan.
  • NEWS2 score with risk band and suggested response, saved with the record and the printout.
  • Shock Index, and a normal, abnormal or critical tag on every vital sign.
  • An allergy banner, drug-allergy warnings and a before-you-finish checklist.
  • Ready for review, approved and locked states, with a time-stamped log.
  • Nothing depends on a connection, so Wi-Fi dead spots do not stop documentation.

Planned with partners: accounts and roles, one server that we host or that runs inside your hospital network with OIDC or SAML sign-in, encrypted storage and FHIR export. These come after the teaching product is strong, and we want hospital teams to shape them.

Home/Privacy and safety

Records stay on the device. Checks stay out of your way.

What we store, what we do not, and how the safety checks behave. We would rather show the gaps than hide them.

Light or dark? The screens follow this site's theme. Use the Theme button at the top of any page to switch.

Patient records stay on the device

The app has no patient database of ours behind it, and it loads no outside services while you work.

Nothing is sent to us

Records are saved in the browser on the device where they were typed. Moving a record to another device is a file you choose to download and upload.

Offline by design

After the first load, the app and all its medical content are kept on the device. No connection is needed to take a history or save a record.

Locks and backups

A PIN lock and privacy screen hide records when the screen is left open. Backups are files you control, with reminders when one is due.

Be clear about what is not here yet. Encryption of stored records and shared hospital databases are not in the app today; both are on the roadmap. Until they are, use device encryption and a screen lock on any device that holds real patient data. Institutions should use fictional cases for teaching. HistoryOsis is documentation and decision-support software. It is not a diagnostic device.

Safety checks that never get in the way

Every check is advisory. It informs the clinician, asks for confirmation where it matters, and never blocks saving.

See the sick patient sooner

  • Respiratory rate, SpO₂ (including Scale 2), blood pressure, pulse, temperature and GCS.
  • Shock Index and BMI worked out for you.
  • Tags use words as well as colour, so they work for everyone.

Decision support only. Every check is advisory and never blocks saving. Clinical judgement and local protocols apply.

Home/Roadmap

Where HistoryOsis is today, and where it is going

Education first, then institutions, then wider clinical depth. Plans are plans, not promises of dates.

What works now, and what we build next

We would rather show you the gaps than hide them. Education comes first, then institutions, then wider clinical depth. Partners help decide the order inside each phase. Last updated November 2026.

Working now

  • History with tap-to-answer questions76 complaints, red flags, templates and carry-forward from earlier records.
  • Vitals, NEWS2 and drug-allergy checksAdvisory warnings that never block saving.
  • Records that are easy to useSummary, print, EMR text, search, tags, versions, trash and backups.
  • Supervisor review and sign-offComments, ready, approved and locked, with a log.
  • Examination chips and differentials23 systems of tap chips, and a rule-based differential for all 76 complaints.
  • Discharge summary and lab flagsEditable discharge screen with print, PDF and text export, and analyte range flags.
  • Offline install, appearance and accessibilityHome-screen app, eight colour presets, High contrast, 400% zoom and screen-reader support.

In development now

  • Clinician review of every systemExamination and differential content is cited and written from standard teaching. Nothing ships as final until a named clinician has signed off that system.
  • Coverage score and practice casesWhich expected questions were never asked, and fictional cases with an OSCE timer.
  • Open beta feedbackEdge cases from students and clinicians decide what we fix first.
Phase A

Examination guidance

So a student never forgets an examination step.

  • Done: tap chips for 23 systems with red-flag alerts
  • Next: step-by-step coach screen and Guide, Practice and Quick modes
  • Each system reviewed by a named clinician before it is called final
Phase B

Learning and assessment

What a university needs to teach with it.

  • History coverage score: which expected questions were never asked
  • About 20 fictional practice cases with an OSCE timer and marking checklist
  • Short recall quizzes on red flags and examination steps
  • Student logbook with supervisor sign-off and a portfolio report
Phase C

Foundations for institutions

So a whole school or hospital can run it.

  • UK and US settings for units, spelling, drug names and early-warning scores
  • Encrypted storage with a passphrase
  • Accounts and roles for students, supervisors and admins, with hospital single sign-on (OIDC or SAML)
  • One server, hosted by us or inside your network, with offline sync and an audit log
  • Cohort dashboard for teachers, and a browser content editor with clinician sign-off
  • Retention, export and deletion on request
Phase D

Clinical depth

What makes it a fuller record for clinics and hospitals.

  • More specialties: paediatrics, obstetrics, psychiatry, emergency
  • Paediatric reference ranges for lab values
  • Problem list
  • Referral letter and a searchable ICD-10 list
  • FHIR export, Urdu and bilingual output, tablet and ward-list layouts
  • Tamper-evident audit trail and electronic signature

Education first

Medical students and universities are our first customers. Clinics and teaching hospitals follow once the teaching product is strong.

No AI for now

We are not building an AI virtual patient, AI drafting or AI coding at this stage. ICD-10 will be a searchable list, and the clinician always chooses the code.

Clinicians sign off content

We draft and cite. A named clinician reviews each body system before it is shown as final. Until then it is labelled as draft.

Plans are plans, not promises of dates. Anything not listed under "Working now" is not in the app today.

UK first, built so the US is not a rewrite

We are starting in the UK and keeping units, spelling, drug names, date formats and the early-warning score switchable for each organisation, so another market is a setting and not a rebuild.

United Kingdom

  • UK GDPRData protection for any personal data we hold.
  • MHRAAssessment of whether the software counts as a medical device.
  • NHS clinical safety, DCB0129 and DCB0160Safety case and hazard log for health IT.
  • NHS Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC)The checklist NHS buyers use for digital tools.

United States

  • HIPAAWith business associate agreements where we host real patient data.
  • FDA clinical decision support guidanceFor checks such as early-warning scores and allergy alerts.
  • FERPAStudent education records.
  • WCAG 2.2 AA and a VPATAccessibility documentation that universities ask for.

What this list is. These are the standards we are designing towards, not certifications we hold. We will confirm with a regulatory adviser which apply before any pilot, and real-patient use by institutions stays switched off until that work is done. In the meantime the checks are advisory, they never block saving, and teaching uses fictional cases.

Open beta: help us make it safer and sharper

HistoryOsis is in open beta and gets better with every real-world edge case. We are inviting three groups to work with us.

Home/Questions

Questions institutions ask

Short answers, written plainly. If yours is missing, write to us and we will add it.

Can I try it without installing or signing up?

Yes. Open the live app in your browser and start a patient. There is no account. If you like it, add it to your home screen for offline use.

How does the differential diagnosis work?

It is a rule-based engine, not AI. It weighs your history chips, red flags, examination findings, vitals, flagged lab values, risk factors, age and sex against a written rule set for each of the 76 complaints. It always lists Must-not-miss causes first. The output is possibilities to consider, not a diagnosis, and the content is draft until clinician review.

Does it need the internet?

Only to load it the first time, and again after an update. After that it runs fully offline, including all medical content.

Where is patient data stored?

In the browser on the device where it was entered. Nothing is sent to HistoryOsis Technologies. You can download a backup file and upload it on another device.

Can a clinic use it as its EMR today?

For a single-device record, yes: structured notes, print, EMR text, search and backups. It does not yet share records between devices or staff, and storage is not encrypted by the app. Institutions should keep teaching to fictional cases until encryption, accounts and the compliance work are done. Hospitals that need shared records should talk to us about a pilot.

Is it a medical device?

We build it as documentation and decision-support software. Its checks are advisory, they never block saving, and the clinician stays responsible for every decision. Because the early-warning score and allergy alerts come closest to advising a clinician, we will confirm the regulatory position with an adviser before any pilot that uses real patient data.

Will you add AI?

Not at this stage. The differential engine is rule-based. We are not building an AI virtual patient, AI drafting or AI diagnosis coding. We are putting our effort into examination guidance, assessment tools and institution features first.

Can we host it ourselves?

That is planned. The same server is designed to run as our hosted service or inside a hospital network, with sign-in through your OIDC or SAML provider. It is not available yet; the app today runs on each device with no server.

Which countries do you support?

We are starting with the United Kingdom, with US settings designed in from the start. The app is in English. Units, drug names and early-warning scores are being made switchable per organisation. Urdu and bilingual output are on the roadmap.

Can we use our own complaints, checklists and templates?

Yes. All medical content sits in one readable file, with a guide for adding complaints, examination systems, investigations and templates. When the app starts it checks that file and says in plain words what is wrong, instead of failing silently.

How is it tested?

Automated checks cover the calculations (BMI, Shock Index, NEWS2, lab flags), the differential rules and their vignettes, data validation, file import, record migration and colour contrast. It runs in any browser. The app is also tested on phone-sized screens, in dark mode and with a keyboard.

What does it cost?

We are choosing our first pilot partners now. Write to us with your institution and what you need, and we will come back with options.
